name: Puzzles & Brain Games
examples: Selected puzzle families and types. Some activities combine several families.

name: Word & language
examples: Solve challenges involving letters, words and language.

name: Number puzzles
examples: Solve numerical constraints or arithmetic challenges.

name: Logic, deduction & strategy
examples: Infer solutions from clues, reason through rules or plan possible moves.

name: Spatial & mechanical
examples: Assemble, move or manipulate pieces.

name: Matching & arrangement
examples: Match, sort, merge or place pieces to reach a goal.

name: Physics & environmental
examples: Use physical interactions, explore environments or navigate routes.

name: Escape & investigation experiences
examples: Experiences combining linked clues and several puzzle mechanics. These may overlap other families.

name: Crosswords
examples: Standard crosswords; cryptic crosswords.

name: Anagrams
examples: Rearrange letters into another word. Example: LISTEN → SILENT.

name: Word guessing
examples: Example: Wordle.

name: Word searches
examples: Find hidden words in a grid of letters.

name: Number placement
examples: Example: Sudoku. Place numbers while satisfying row, column and region rules.

name: Arithmetic puzzles
examples: Example: Kakuro. Fill cells with numbers that satisfy sum clues.

name: Logic-grid puzzles
examples: Use clues to match people, objects, places or times.

name: Deduction mysteries
examples: Murder mysteries: compare evidence, statements and alibis to identify a culprit.

name: Logic riddles
examples: Solve a short reasoning problem. This includes reasoning-based riddles rather than all wordplay riddles.

name: Strategy puzzles
examples: Chess puzzles: find a move or sequence while considering the opponent’s possible responses.

name: Assembly puzzles
examples: Jigsaws; tangrams. Fit pieces together to form a picture or shape.

name: Sliding puzzles
examples: Sliding-tile puzzles: move pieces through available spaces to reach a target arrangement.

name: Mechanical manipulation
examples: Rubik’s cube; interlocking puzzles.

name: Swap
examples: Swap adjacent pieces to create matches. Example: Candy Crush Saga.

name: Blast
examples: Tap a group of matching coloured tiles to clear it.

name: Chain
examples: Connect matching pieces into a chain to remove them.

name: Pair
examples: Find and remove matching pairs of tiles or pieces.

name: Sort
examples: Sort mixed coloured objects or liquids into the required groups.

name: Merge
examples: Combine compatible pieces into a new or upgraded piece.

name: Block placement
examples: Place blocks into a grid to complete rows or columns.

name: Physics puzzles
examples: Manipulate ropes, balls or blocks using physical interactions.

name: Environmental puzzles
examples: Explore an environment and manipulate objects to solve challenges.

name: Mazes
examples: Find a route through passages, obstacles and dead ends.

name: Physical escape rooms
examples: Work through linked clues and tasks in a physical space. May combine deduction, number, word and mechanical puzzles.

name: Digital escape games
examples: Explore a digital setting, investigate objects and solve linked puzzles to progress or escape.
